vision_features.image_context: Close-up ground-level view of a young soybean plant in a field. A human hand is visible in the upper right corner, appearing to hold or manipulate the plant for examination. vision_features.abnormalities:
1. Lower leaves and cotyledons: The leaves at the base of the plant are completely collapsed and dried, papery in texture, tan to light brown in color, shriveled and curled inward. These appear medium to large in size relative to the seedling stage. No distinct border coloration — the entire leaf tissue is uniformly pale tan/beige and dry.
2. Stem base (hypocotyl area): The stem near the soil line appears constricted or pinched, noticeably narrower than the upper stem. The tissue at this zone appears darker brown, dry, and shrunken compared to the green tissue of the upper stem. This affected zone spans approximately 10–20 mm vertically.
3. Lower stem and root crown: At the soil level, there is a visibly collapsed, wrinkled, brownish structure that appears to be the remains of the seed coat or lower cotyledon tissue — tan, papery, and hollow-looking. The tissue here is crinkled and collapsed.
4. Upper stem: The upper portion of the stem remains green, though the plant appears to be wilting overall. The transition from green upper stem to brown/tan lower stem is abrupt.
5. Distribution: The damage is concentrated at and just above the soil line, progressing upward to the lower leaves, while upper growth retains some green coloration.
vision_features.absences:
1. No powdery or fuzzy coating visible on any part of the plant.
2. No distinct circular or angular spots with defined margins on any leaf surface — the leaf damage is whole-leaf collapse rather than localized spots.
3. No visible tiny raised dots, thread-like structures, or pustules on the stem or leaf surfaces.
4. No yellowing (pale green to yellow gradient) present — the affected tissue transitions directly to tan/brown dry color without an intermediate yellow halo or zone.
vision_features.summary: A young soybean seedling displays severe collapse of its lower leaves and cotyledons, which are completely dried, shriveled, and tan-brown in color. The most severely affected area is the stem base at the soil line, where the tissue appears constricted, darkened, and shrunken, with a sharp transition to green tissue above. The lower plant structures are papery and hollow-looking, suggesting the plant has lost vascular function at or near the soil line. The upper stem and newer growth retain green coloration, indicating damage is concentrated at the base. The single most striking visual feature is the abrupt pinching and browning of the stem at the soil line, with the lower leaves and cotyledons fully collapsed into dry, papery remnants.
